ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y_1=k_1x+b$ intersects with the hyperbola $y_2=\frac{k_2}{x} \left(x>0\right)$ at points $A$ and $B$ within the first quadrant. Given $A(1, m)$ and $B(2, 1)$, find the equations of the line and the hyperbola.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given point $B(2, 1)$ is on the hyperbola $y_{2}=\frac{k_{2}}{x}$, \\
$\therefore k_{2}=2\times 1=2$,\\
$\therefore$ the equation of the hyperbola is $y_{2}=\frac{2}{x}$\\
Since $A(1, m)$ is on the hyperbola $y_{2}=\frac{2}{x}$, \\
$\therefore m=\frac{2}{1}=2$,\\
$\therefore A(1, 2)$\\
Since line $y_{1}=k_{1}x+b$ passes through points $A(1, 2)$ and $B(2, 1)$,\\
$\therefore \left\{\begin{array}{l}k_{1}+b=2\\ 2k_{1}+b=1\end{array}\right.$, solving this gives $\left\{\begin{array}{l}k_{1}=-1\\ b=3\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore$ the equation for line $AB$ is $\boxed{y_{1}=-x+3}$.

Since $A(1,m)$ is also on the hyperbola, $m=\frac{2}{1}=2$, so $A(1,2)$. The line $y_1=k_1x+b$ passes through $A(1,2)$ and $B(2,1)$, so $\begin{cases}k_1+b=2\\2k_1+b=1\end{cases}$, which gives $k_1=-1$ and $b=3$. Therefore, the line is $y_1=-x+3$, and the hyperbola is $y_2=\frac{2}{x}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system; in the first quadrant, a straight line slanting downward to the right and a decreasing hyperbola are drawn. The two curves intersect at two points A and B, where A is at the upper left, B is at the lower right, and both are located in the first quadrant.

Then reason: Because A(1,m) and B(2,1) are both intersection points of the straight line y_1=k_1x+b and the hyperbola y_2=k_2/x, they are both on the hyperbola and also both on the straight line. First substitute B(2,1) into the hyperbola y_2=k_2/x, obtaining 1=k_2/2, therefore k_2=2, so the equation of the hyperbola is y_2=2/x. Then substitute A(1,m) into this hyperbola, obtaining m=2/1=2, so A=(1,2). The straight line passes through A(1,2) and B(2,1), and the slope k_1=(1-2)/(2-1)=-1. Substitute A(1,2) into y_1=-x+b, obtaining 2=-1+b, so b=3. Therefore the equation of the straight line is y_1=-x+3, and the equation of the hyperbola is y_2=2/x.
